content: The company was founded by renowned professor and dancer Leonardo Martínez Moya. A group of former dancers and masters of the Conjunto Folklórico Nacional de Cuba, from different generations, came together to give birth to this project.

The objective is to promote, share and preserve the knowledge of traditional folkloric Cuban dances. For this group of masters it is an honour to work with passionate dancers and musicians from around the world who, through their love of Cuban culture, have joined them on this magical journey through dance, song and music. The company is directed by Leonardo Martínez Moya and Giuliana Cassarisi.

It is also a tribute to the Cuban people, their culture, their diverse ethnicity, and the legacy of all the masters, dancers, musicians and artists before them who spread Cuban culture around the world. In Cuba, the Conjunto Folklórico Nacional de Cuba has represented the island's heritage through dance and performance since 1962.
The company brings together dancers from all over the world, united by their passion for Cuban dance and culture.
Every month we meet in a different city in Europe for an intensive training weekend.
A strong emphasis on the development of our members, with high-level academic and choreographic programmes.
We perform at festivals, cultural events and tours, highlighting the richness and diversity of Cuban culture.
We collaborate with renowned artists, choreographers and musicians to create productions that blend tradition with modern expression.
Workshops and activities that engage local communities wherever we perform, creating real opportunities for cultural exchange.

The International Company of Cuban Dances is dedicated to preserving and promoting Cuban culture by safeguarding and sharing Cuba's artistic and cultural traditions through performances, workshops and international collaborations.

Education and training are at the heart of our work. We offer dedicated programmes for dancers, passing on Cuban dance techniques and the values of folklore to new generations across Europe and beyond.

We are also committed to the research and documentation of traditional Cuban dances, carefully recording choreographies, music and costumes to ensure their preservation and transmission for the future.

A key objective is to foster integration and exchange between Cuba and other countries, through international festivals and collaborations with other dance companies, and to recognise and celebrate the African roots of Cuban culture. We are proud to be the official European representation of the Conjunto Folklórico Nacional de Cuba. With our Encuentros we travel to Havana to train with the maestros of the Conjunto and the Conjunto Ban Rarrá: two intensive weeks in 2024 and 2025, including the Conjunto's anniversary show.

The academy is open to everyone joining us for the first time. Study Afro-Cuban dances in depth at your own rhythm. Stay in the academy if your main goal is to train and grow as a dancer, or if you can't join every month.

Become a member of the company and perform on stages across Europe. After at least three training weekends, the teachers decide whether you join the company or continue in the academy a little longer. Members commit to attending every month and rehearsing the choreographies.
What is the International Company of Cuban Dances?

The company was founded in 2022. We are a team of dancers from around Europe who are passionate about traditional Afro-Cuban dances. Our goal is to train and perform the traditional folkloric Cuban dances outside of Cuba. Find out more about our teachers on the About page, and get an impression of our classes on Instagram.
How can I join the Academy?

The academy is open to everyone who wants to join us for the first time. You are welcome to continue in the academy if you don't feel ready to perform yet, or if you can't join very regularly. If your main goal is simply to train and become better at Afro-Cuban dances, you can stay as a student of the academy.
How can I join the Company?

There is no formal audition day. The audition happens over the course of several training weekends once you have shown an interest in joining: just mention it to Leonardo or one of the members of the organisation. You attend a minimum of three weekends, taking part in the academy classes while the teachers watch you dance and assess your level. After those three sessions the teachers decide whether you join the company or continue in the academy a while longer.

These are not beginner classes. You need prior knowledge of Afro-Cuban dances: Yoruba, Arará, Palo, Makuta, Yuka and Rumba. The training does not cover basic steps or rhythms, so it's best if you have taken at least two years of classes, or have enough basic training to follow along. This applies to both academy and company members.
I am a teacher, do I have to audition?
Yes, everyone goes through the same process. We appreciate that many of you have danced for years and are teachers yourselves, but the process has to be fair, so it's the same for everyone.
Where do the trainings take place?
In a different European city every month, thanks to the help of our students. Check the Trainings page for the next dates and venues.

Leonardo Moya, Sergio Larrinaga, Arelys Savón and Mireisi Morales, all former dancers of the Conjunto Folklórico Nacional de Cuba, who also trained there. For the 2026–2027 season they are joined by Javier Monier and Federico Nuñez.
How long are the training weekends?

About 10 hours of classes over two days. Trainings usually start on Saturday around noon or 1 pm and finish around 5 pm on Sunday, so everyone has time to travel. The full schedule is published one week before each training.
What do you do during the trainings?

Usually a combination of chants, Yoruba technique and specific orishas, Palo, Arará and Rumba, plus traditional popular dances such as mambo, cha-cha-chá and son, with live percussion. It varies from weekend to weekend. Company members also rehearse the choreographies for our shows.
We continue to perform our show Raíces Cubanas in different places across Europe, along with smaller performances and festival appearances during the year. We are always open to new opportunities.
What is the level of commitment for company members?

Once you are in the company and working towards a performance, we ask you to attend every month (you can miss only one training, or discuss it with the teachers). You commit to learning the choreographies and practising on your own so we make the best use of our time together. Everyone performs in more than one choreography.
What does it cost and how do I sign up?
Tickets and ICCD t-shirts are sold on Weezevent. Early-bird tickets are the cheapest, and we always announce until when they are available.
Do I need to arrange my own accommodation?

Yes, everyone organises their own travel and accommodation. You're welcome to arrange to travel with other participants privately. If anything special is organised for a weekend, you'll hear about it in our WhatsApp group.
Who can I contact with more questions?
Join our WhatsApp group or send us a message on Instagram, we're happy to help.

The company is directed by Leonardo Martínez Moya and Giuliana Cassarisi, together with a team of dancers who organise the trainings, shows and travels.

We are a team of dancers from around Europe, united by our passion and love for Afro-Cuban dances. Our goal is to perform the traditional Cuban dances outside of Cuba, thereby preserving Cuba's rich folkloric traditions.
Live drums and voices are the heartbeat of every training and every show. These are the musicians who accompanied our first performance at the Arca Social Club in Rome on 25 May 2024.
A 90-minute dance-theatre show in two parts

The sound of the waters echoes through the myths and legends that shape Cuban identity. The many cultural currents that coexist on the island come together to form the soul of its people. Rebellious, joyful, musical and united, these qualities reflect the true spirit of Cuba.

Raíces Cubanas, presented by the Generación Abbilona Association and its International Folkloric Company of Traditional Cuban Dances, brings this spirit to the stage. The performance is a journey through musical and dance traditions of African and Cuban origin, tracing the richness of Cuban culture from the colonial era to the present day.

The first part explores the Afro-Cuban religious and mythological world. It highlights the influence of the orishas and other African deities on Cuban culture, with choreographies dedicated to Elegguá, Ogún, Yemayá, Changó and Oyá, as well as a portrayal of the journey of enslaved Africans to Cuba. It shows how their spiritual beliefs and musical traditions became a fundamental part of Cuban identity.

The second part celebrates the popular music and dance genres born from the birth of the Cuban Republic up to the present day: danzón, mambo, cha-cha-chá, son, the street vendors' chants (pregones), rumba and the Cuban carnival. It highlights the racial and cultural blending that sets Cuba apart and celebrates the joy and diversity of the Cuban people.

ICCD is a collective of dancers, teachers and culture-bearers rooted in the legacy of the Conjunto Folklórico Nacional de Cuba. Founded in 2022 by former dancers and teachers of the Conjunto, we train, perform and build community around Afro-Cuban dance and tradition, with love, depth and rhythm. Our goal is to keep these folkloric traditions alive outside of Cuba and to share them with new generations.
Come for the dance. Stay for the family.
More than a company, a family

We came from different countries, with different stories, but one passion brought us together: Cuban culture and dance. We started by learning steps. We ended up building a family. We laugh together, struggle together, make sacrifices together, and when things get difficult, we stay united. No ego. No competition. Just passion, friendship and a shared mission: to keep Cuban culture alive and share it with the world.

Leonardo graduated from the Escuela Nacional de Arte (ENA) and the Instituto Superior de Arte (ISA) and became principal dancer at the Conjunto Folklórico Nacional de Cuba, where he danced for 25 years. As choreographer and professor at the Conjunto he created two important pieces: Moforibale a Changó and Ochanigue.

He arrived in Italy in 2008 and has been teaching and choreographing ever since, touring more than 30 countries around the world and promoting Cuban culture through Proyecto Lucumí. Today he teaches contemporary and Cuban folkloric technique, Afro-Cuban dances (Yoruba, Congo, Arará, Abakuá, Bantú), popular Cuban dances (Son, Mambo, Cha-cha-chá), Rumba (Yambú, Guaguancó, Columbia), dances campesinas, African-Haitian dances and Cuban salsa (Timba, Rueda de Casino).

Arelys is a graduate of the Escuela Nacional de Arte and the Instituto Superior de Arte (ISA) in Cuba. She was a soloist and teacher of the Conjunto Folklórico Nacional de Cuba, touring Europe, Japan, Mexico, the Dominican Republic, the United States and many other countries, and took part in television programmes, films and modelling work.

Since 2004 she has lived in Italy, where she is a member of the Italian Federation of Sports Dance and serves as a competition judge. She is a first-class MIDAS – ASC Danza teacher, contributing to the training, promotion and development of Cuban culture in Italy and across Europe.

Sergio was principal dancer and choreographer at the Conjunto Folklórico Nacional de Cuba. Over his long career he was also teacher and choreographer at the Teatro América in Havana, and director and choreographer of the company Yoruba Andabo, among much more.

He now lives in Italy, where he is a member of the Federazione Professionale di Danza (FPD), and continues to teach Cuban and Afro-Cuban dances around the world.

Mireisi is a former dancer of the Conjunto Folklórico Nacional de Cuba. As choreographer and teacher of the company she leads technique and Orisha classes at our monthly trainings, passing on the knowledge, expression and musicality of Cuba's folkloric tradition.

Train with ICCD and dive into the heart of Cuban folklore. Led by former masters of the Conjunto Folklórico Nacional de Cuba, these weekends are a rare chance to go deep into Afro-Cuban dance and music with live percussion and chants. More than a workshop, it is a full cultural immersion.

These trainings are designed for intermediate to advanced dancers looking for meaningful growth and a deeper connection to Cuban folkloric dance and music. They are not beginner classes: a basic knowledge of Yoruba, Arará, Palo, Makuta, Yuka and Rumba is expected.
10 hours of classes over 2 days (Saturday & Sunday)
